small_guidance:
- The current gather-based ConvTranspose2d does redundant work: for stride=2, only 1/4 of (kh,kw) combinations are valid per output pixel, but the inner static loop still issues all 16 (kh,kw) loads. Split the kernel into 4 sub-kernels (or use stride-aware indexing) keyed on (oh%2, ow%2) so each output only loops over the (KH/STRIDE)*(KW/STRIDE)=2*2=4 valid taps instead of 16 — a ~4x reduction in loads and dot work.
- Tile the spatial dimension on contiguous OW rows (e.g. BLOCK_OW=64, BLOCK_OH=1 or 2) instead of flattening OH*OW; this makes `iw` contiguous and lets x-loads coalesce across BLOCK_SP for fixed ih. Add autotune configs with BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_OW=128, num_warps=8, num_stages=3.
- Cache the permuted weight (`_weight_t`) once in __init__ as a registered buffer rather than recomputing `.permute().contiguous()` every forward call.
large_guidance:
- Switch from a gather (input-stationary at output) to a scatter-add formulation: one program per (N, IC tile, IH*IW tile) loads x once, computes the outer product with weight[ic, oc, kh, kw], and atomically (or via deterministic accumulation buffers) adds into the appropriate output locations. With stride=2 the scatter pattern is dense in the output and avoids the divide/modulo guard on every tap.
- Alternative: implicit-GEMM with K = IC and M = OC (small, =64), N = output tile. Since IC=OC=64 are both small, treat this as 4 independent stride-phase GEMMs of shape (OC=64) x (IC=64) x (N tile), one per (kh%stride, kw%stride) phase — each phase writes a disjoint sub-grid of the output, no atomics needed, and you can fuse bias-subtract + tanh in the epilogue.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) layout for both x and out so the IC/OC axis is the contiguous one in the GEMM-K and GEMM-M dimensions; pre-permute x in forward (cheap vs the conv) and store NHWC, permuting back only if needed.
